message.content: This is a check that session capture works in this repo. Read CLAUDE.md, then reply in one sentence with the judging weights it lists. Do not edit any files.

content.content:
1	# Digital Life hackathon project
2	
3	Hackathon entry: build an artificial system that shows a meaningful property of life (autonomy, persistence, adaptation, interaction, emergence). Depth in one property beats coverage of five. The repo is the submission and will be public.
4	
5	Judging: technical depth 30%, originality 25%, demonstrated behaviour and experimentation 20%, engineering and reproducibility 15%, effective and transparent tool use including AI 10%. Judges do not reward the biggest model, most tokens, most agents or fanciest frontend. They do reward a sound negative result over an unsupported claim of emergence.
6	
7	## Everything here is published
8	
9	- Every session in this repo is exported to agent_traces/ by a hook (tools/export_traces.py) and committed to a public repo. The export drops model reasoning, harness-injected context and secrets. The prompts, replies, tool calls and tool results are kept and published.
10	- Keep sessions on this project. Do not bring in private company material, client or investor information, or other workspaces' content. If something private comes up, add the term to agent_traces/.redact-terms.
11	- Never print or echo secrets. Keys live in .env (gitignored), read by name. Document new variables in .env.example.
12	
13	## Evidence rules
14	
15	The evidence docs (EXPERIMENTS.md, AI_DISCLOSURE.md, DECISIONS.md, agent_traces/) report what happened, including failures. The README can tell the story with energy, but every claim in it points at an experiment or a run directory.
16	
17	- Run experiments only through `experiments/run.py` with a committed config and at least three seeds. Commit before a run you plan to cite.
18	- Never call a behaviour emergent until the controls in EXPERIMENTS.md "Protocol" have been run: ablate the credited mechanism, compare against a random or shuffled baseline, vary prompts (if an LLM is involved), and vary the setup.
19	- Never invent or round up a number. Quote results with n and spread, straight from experiments/results/.
20	- Record failed experiments the same day under "Negative results".
21	- When an agent proposes a design choice, log it in DECISIONS.md as an agent proposal. The human who accepts it is named only when they actually do.
22	
23	## Working rules
24	
25	- Commit small and often, with messages saying what changed. Never squash, amend published commits or rewrite history.
26	- Commit the exported agent_traces/ changes along with the work they produced.
27	- `make test` before each commit that touches src/, experiments/ or tools/.
28	- `make check` runs the submission checklist. Every FAIL must be fixed before submission.
29	- The humans must be able to explain every mechanism. When building something non-obvious, add a short plain explanation to ARCHITECTURE.md as you go.
30	
31	## Layout
32	
33	- src/digital_life/: the system. runlog.py and smoke.py are scaffold.
34	- experiments/: run.py, configurations/*.toml, results/ (committed, keep small), analysis/.
35	- agent_traces/: exported sessions, events, INDEX.md (generated); README.md and summaries/ (hand-written, labelled as such).
36	- tools/: trace export, presubmit check, secret patterns, git hooks.
37	- demo/: screenshots and recordings. `make demo` must reproduce a small version.
38

content.text: The judging weights in CLAUDE.md are technical depth 30%, originality 25%, demonstrated behaviour and experimentation 20%, engineering and reproducibility 15%, and effective and transparent tool use including AI 10%.
